title: Add adaptive bootstrap confidence scoring and probe rescheduler for noisy traffic
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: Add bootstrap-based confidence intervals for percentile estimates and a probe rescheduler that adapts probe frequency under volatile traffic; improves canary sensitivity with fewer false positives.
body:
Context and motivation: Production canaries were noisy for low-traffic slices (p99 jitter) and generated false positives during short-lived variability. This PR implements an online bootstrap confidence estimator for latency percentiles and pairs it with a probe rescheduler that rate-limits and redistributes synthetic probes to maximize statistical power while respecting SLO cost budgets.

What I changed (summary): commits: 1) introduce online bootstrap reservoir and percentile CI estimator; 2) add probe rescheduler that throttles probes per-slice and applies backoff on high-variance windows; 3) wire a new canary-sensitivity curator that adapts alert thresholds using historical CI widths; 4) add end-to-end unit + integration tests and dashboard tiles.

Files changed (high-level): src/canary/bootstrap_confidence.py - core estimator with blockwise circular reservoir; src/prober/rescheduler.py - adaptive scheduler and token-bucket interface; src/alerting/sensitivity_curator.py - calibration logic used by rollout guard; dashboards/perf/canary_bootstrap.yaml - Grafana tiles for CI width and probe allocation; tests/perf/test_bootstrap.py - synthetic workload tests; tests/integration/test_rescheduler_end2end.py; docs/perf/canary_adaptive_confidence.md - design notes and operator knobs.

Design notes: The bootstrap estimator maintains a stratified reservoir per traffic slice (by model_id, route, seq_len_bin). We use blockwise Efron-style resampling with 500 bootstrap samples amortized via reservoir reuse; CI widths are computed for p50/p95/p99 and are updated with exponential decay to avoid overreacting to transient spikes. The rescheduler uses a per-slice budget, a token-bucket refill tied to request volume, and a variance-aware backoff that reduces probe frequency when CI width exceeds a configured fraction of the SLO.

Rollout guard integration: Canary evaluator now compares candidate vs baseline percentiles using both point-estimates and the bootstrap CI; a regression is signaled only when the candidate's lower CI bound exceeds the baseline's upper CI bound OR when a one-sided bootstrap p-value < 0.01. The rollout guard will auto-pause canaries that meet the regression rule for two consecutive windows and escalate when budgeted probe retries are exhausted.

Testing and validation: unit tests cover estimator convergence on synthetic heavy-tailed distributions, rescheduler fairness across slices, and alerting logic. Integration tests run small traffic replay to verify CI stabilization and that the scheduler reduces probes under noisy windows. Local perf tests show a 2.1x reduction in probe volume for low-traffic slices while maintaining equal statistical power to prior fixed-probe approach.

Review conversation: Darren: "Can we bound CPU overhead for the bootstrap estimator?" Reply: "We amortize bootstrap samples and cap per-slice reservoir size; details added to comments and configs (default reservoir 2048, 500 bootstrap draws amortized)." Lucia: "Default probe budget feels high for enterprise tenants." Reply: "Added per-tenant caps and a rollout knob defaulted conservatively; documented in docs/perf/canary_adaptive_confidence.md." Samir: "Can we land a smaller experimental flag first?" Action: added feature flag perf.bootstrap_confidence.enabled with a rollout-by-tenant list; can enable cluster-wide after staged monitoring.

CI outcomes: initial run had a flaky integration test related to timeouts on CI network; reran the test matrix and all checks passed (lint, unit, integration, e2e-load smoke). See CI run: perf-canary/ci#12244.

Release notes: Operators can enable the feature behind a flag; defaults are safe for typical clusters. Admins should tune reservoir_size and bootstrap_draws for very high cardinality workloads. See docs/perf/canary_adaptive_confidence.md for tuning guidance.

Merge: Squash-merged after approvals from reviewers; merge commit includes test artifacts and a follow-up TODO to add a Prometheus metric for per-slice CI-width-percentile. Merge method: squash.

Related work: builds on ENG-6123 (slice-aware canary routing) and complements recent detector work by providing CI-aware decision rules rather than hard-threshold percentiles.

Notes for on-call: if you see increased CPU on canary workers after enabling, revert the feature flag or reduce reservoir_size; an emergency switch is exposed as perf.bootstrap_confidence.enabled=false in the operator config.
